posts.meta_description:
shivya on July 4, 2026: "It’s been two months since this piece of my heart - my second book, Rootless and Restless - was released into the world (well, India)!
 
How do I feel?
 
Vulnerable, emotional, overwhelmed, anxious, grateful, hopeful, like an imposter ☺️
 
I have nothing but gratitude in my heart:
 
👉🏼 For the messages I’ve been receiving pretty much every day on how my stories in Rootless and Restless have moved and inspired you, impacted your life and travel choices, and nudged you to think about how we show up in the world.
 
👉🏼 For readers who, after finishing the book, bought extra copies to gift to best friends, sisters and the world-curious in your lives 🌸
 
👉🏼 For entrepreneurs who gifted the book at their alternative, nature-centric, yoga-based, fitness and travel retreats.
 
👉🏼 For independent bookstores and alternative spaces (eco clothing outlets, upcycling stores, vegan cafes) stocking the book for sale for their conscious communities!
 
👉🏼 For readers who feel driven to think about the fragile beauty of our planet and how it can be protected, after reading the book 🥹
 
👉🏼 For everyone who’s shared the book with your friends and networks, recommended it to your book club, posted about it on social media, reviewed it on Amazon / Goodreads and spotlighted it on your newsletter and blog 🙏
 
In a world where a new book is published every 8 seconds (CRAZY, I KNOW), I’m so glad Rootless and Restless found you 💚

Two months in, it still holds the bestseller tag on Amazon India in multiple categories ☺️

PS: Thanks @dil.cine.drone @subodhUniyaal @natasha_gupta @akshitajainphotography @amitgaikwad191 and others for these beautiful photos!".

posts.meta_description:
shivya on October 6, 2026: "BANGALORE, thank you for making the launch of my new book Rootless and Restless extra special 💚
 
When I first started thinking about my book tour, the first place I imagined doing it was a collaborative creative space that felt like the perfect extension of my values – a female-owned independent bookstore @champacabooks, my favorite plant-based café in the country @copperandcloves, a zero waste organic clothing store that is half my wardrobe @nonasties , and a thrift store that gives a new lease of life to used clothes @lovemetwice_vintageandthrift … and I’m so glad we could make it happen there! 
 
👉🏼 I loved being in conversation with @vasanthihariprakash. When we connected for the first time before the launch, it felt like we had known each other a long time with so much in common. Thank you for bringing your beautiful questions, insights and energy to the evening (and also reading the book in record time 😉).
 
👉🏼 I’m so grateful to the awesome team behind @champacabooks ; thank you for such a stunning curation of books, and for giving space to my work on your shelves!
 
👉🏼 All my gratitude to the @copperandcloves team for staying open late for us, and treating our tastebuds to your delicious, healthy, thoughtfully-sourced culinary creations.

👉🏼 Big thank you @dil.cine.foto.drone for your soulful photography! 
 
👉🏼 And most of all, I’m so grateful to each one of you for joining us that evening, bringing so much warmth, love and curiosity into the room. Thanks for waiting patiently during the long book signing, your thoughtful notes and cards, and all the fleeting conversations 🥹
 
I’m now planning the next leg of my book tour in India from end October to mid December – speaking at literature festivals, book clubs and universities. If you have ideas to host a talk or event on the themes of conscious travel, living with local communities and climate action, please reach out 🌸".

posts.meta_description:
180 likes, 9 comments - readwithak_ on October 1, 2026: "@shivya

Sometimes we choose our path in life and sometimes life chooses it for us. In my opinion this line is the most accurate and relatable to most of our lives, if I can say so on behalf of others too. This book opens with a very haunting meditation on departure, identity, and belonging, where travel becomes an encounter with fear, memory, and transformation. 

This is an adventure travel memoir where I found a person slowly discovering that movement and freedom are not always the same thing. The farther Shivya Nath travels, the less the book seems interested in geography and the more it begins asking a question: what exactly are we running towards when we keep leaving?

I loved the contradictions at the heart of her journey. She leaves the office because routine feels like confinement, (I too feel the same personally, but so far, I am not able to gather that courage so I can leave it. Hope one day I will be.) then leaves cities for forests, islands, and mountains, only to discover that even freedom can become another kind of restlessness. Robinson Crusoe Island becomes a wound when she leaves it. Patagonia becomes beautiful and unbearable at once. Goa teaches her slowness. The pandemic takes travel away and forces her to discover that a life cannot depend entirely on the next horizon.

The book also refuses to romanticise travel and in my opinion that makes it a unique book in its category apart from the other things. The farther she goes, the more she becomes aware of what travel costs, not only in money or comfort but in carbon, consumption, privilege and the lives of the places being visited. That self-questioning gives the journey a moral weight without turning it into a lecture. Her decision to study sustainability feels less like a new chapter and more like the natural consequence of everything she had already experienced.

And then comes the strange realisation that perhaps the traveller she had spent years trying to become was also someone she eventually had to outgrow. The final movement towards a slower, more rooted life in the Himalayas does not feel like surrender. 

..in comments".

posts.meta_description:
shivya on September 29, 2026: "Delighted to share that I’ll be the official climate storyteller at the upcoming @bangkokclimateactionweek – from 3-10 October 2026!

During this time, parks, public spaces and event venues across the city of Bangkok will turn into Southeast Asia’s largest climate gathering.

Besides policymakers and climate scientists, BKKCAW will bring together local communities, city leaders, entrepreneurs, youth, civil society to exchange ideas on climate action.

Think art exhibitions, films, talks and workshops on nature and biodiversity, tourism, energy, urban mobility, food systems, climate adaptation, waste management, education and more.

Follow my stories and posts @shivya to join these inspiring climate conversations virtually!

#BKKCAW #bangkokclimateactionweek #Bangkok #climatestoryteller #climateaction".

posts.meta_description:
shivya on September 27, 2026: "When can we finally stop choosing between our freedom and safety?

When will public spaces be closed to predators instead of us? 

For how long do we need to be outraged before we’re granted our most basic rights?

How many more times will we be told to stay home to protect ourselves? 

When will be able to go out at night without having to watch our backs?

How long will we have to defend our right to wear what we want without being told ‘we’re asking for it?’

When will be able to say goodbye without saying, message me when you get home?

When will we live in a world where questions like this no longer need to be asked?".

posts.meta_description:
shivya on September 21, 2026: "As I walked out of my homestay and crossed the vine-covered yard of the neighbor, her tiny dog barked at me. She ran out, beetroot in hand, dressed all in black. She asked me to come in and offered me sweet pears from her tree.

I walked to the 19th century stone church of Theth, once the unofficial village school. An old guy lay passed out on the sitting area so I sat on the other side. I was lost in thought when he suddenly woke up and started playing his Çifteli!

It was a hot day, so I hiked to a waterfall. I was lucky to share its magic with only a few others. One was a woman from North Macedonia who’d driven over with her family. They motivated me to get into the icy water 🥶
 
By the river, I read a book by a female Albanian writer who wrote that every village had a ‘kulla’ to guard the ‘kanun’ - and just minutes after I left, I noticed a sign leading to a kulla! One of Albania’s last remaining towers where criminals men were kept in custody, and the village council decided their fate 😮

Near it was an ancient stone house. I asked the two kids playing outside if they lived there. One said yes, and I could go in if I unlocked the tight latch on the gate. So I did. Inside we feasted on ripe little red plums on the tree… until the real owner walked out and the kids ran away! I’d been pranked 😬

I saw a shepherd grazing a large flock of sheep on what was once a meadow but is now a camping site! We chatted in Italian (him) and Spanish (me), and with a large smile and open arms, he proclaimed he was a free bird - never married.

I took a detour up a tiny mountain trail. A woman was collecting maize in a bucket, and invited me to her fields, withering in the hot weather. She opened pods of white beans (groshe); I had tried some but had no idea that’s what they looked like uncooked.

Back at my homestay, sitting under the stars, my hostess told me about “besa” - the promise set in the kanun - asking mountain dwellers to shelter, feed and offer raki to all guests. The idea of taking money was insulting. But with tourism, a lot has changed. 

A lot indeed has changed with tourism. But somewhere deeper, fragments of besa still remain 💚".

posts.meta_description:
shivya on September 17, 2026: "Last month, terrifying videos and images of the Nepal floods flooded our feeds.
 
I tried to connect friends of friends searching for missing family members through my tourism networks, and it led to a lot of heartbreak.
 
I followed a lot of the coverage of the floods on social media, international news channels, climate podcasts… and was surprised that hardly anyone was talking about how the loss of lives in these floods is deeply linked to the need for climate justice / climate finance.

Take the time to read this, share it, research further on these topics, because they will define our coming years on this planet 🥹🌏".
